correctness.rationale: The published 2017 near-equal three-primes proof works uniformly for arbitrary prescribed admissible reduced classes modulo its auxiliary product of small primes. Seven explicitly checked distinct unit triples modulo 7, complemented by CRT at all other local primes, force pairwise distinct summands without assuming that the headline theorem itself ensures distinctness. Choosing \(t=4\) or \(t=5\) according to parity gives an odd positive remainder \(R\) with \(t p_j\le R<(t+1)p_{k+1}\); the prime number theorem then ensures all near-equal primes exceed \(p_j\). The primorial envelope of Deléglise–Nicolas gives the product ratio, a parity argument gives the exact branch, and AM–GM gives the factor asymptotic. Finite code serves only as a cross-check.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Matomäki–Maynard–Shao (2017), arXiv:1610.02017, has substantially stronger near-equal ternary prime coverage than classical Vinogradov. Their Theorem 1.1 alone does not require distinctness; the proof of Theorem 2.1 works uniformly for arbitrary admissible reduced residue triples, permitting a new elementary CRT refinement distinguishing all three primes modulo seven. Deléglise–Nicolas (2015) controls bounded-sum H, and neither article states the exact-sum extremal consequences. We do not present the older 2017 input as newly proved.

originality.rationale: PASS with residual risk: original source [1] concerns prime partition enumeration; [2] only bounded-sum prime-product extrema. The 2017 near-equal three-primes theorem and its uniform reduced-class proof furnish a deep input, but the published article does not state the constant-defect distinct-prime packing, parity classification, or product relaxation comparison. It may nevertheless be an implicit short corollary, and prior work inaccessible to the present checks could cover it. Campbell’s distinct-prime result proves unboundedness of a different gap and is not dominating.
residual_risks: The 2017 near-equal-three-primes proof may allow an experienced reader to infer the constant-defect extremal completion quickly; an indexed or unindexed prior corollary could already state it.
Not all older research-history files were accessible for comprehensive deduplication; only actual recovered claims and recorded database/published literature were compared.

value.rationale: PASS: supplies an absolute two-part bound on the natural exact-sum prime packing deficit for every sufficiently large integer, an exact parity-dependent branch, and a polynomial multiplicative relaxation bound comparing an exact-sum maximum product against a bounded-sum maximum product. These are nontrivial and motivated exact-sum extremal consequences of distinctness-enforced analytic prime representations, not an arbitrary numerical slice or known finite table. Sharpness of the universal constants is not claimed.
